high.title: WebView exposes a JavaScript bridge as "Util"
high.description: addJavascriptInterface binds a Java object to the JavaScript name "Util". Any page loaded in this WebView can call its @JavascriptInterface methods: readKey, writeKey. The WebView exposes a JavaScript bridge named 'Util' that provides direct read and write access to the app's 'Settings' SharedPreferences via the `readKey` and `writeKey` methods. Because the WebView loads content over unencrypted HTTP, a remote attacker can perform a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack to inject malicious JavaScript and steal or modify the stored 'API_KEY_SECRET'.
high.impact: If attacker-controlled content ever loads in this WebView, it can invoke these native methods directly.

info.title: No network security config declared
info.description: The app declares neither android:networkSecurityConfig nor usesCleartextTraffic, so it relies on platform defaults and pins no domain. With targetSdkVersion 27 those defaults still permit cleartext HTTP (see the cleartext finding).
info.impact: Without pinning, anyone who gets a CA trusted on the device can read and alter the app's TLS traffic.
info.recommendation: Declare a network security config that disables cleartext and pins the domains that carry sensitive traffic.

reasons: No certificate pinning. Pinning defends against an attacker who already controls a trusted CA or the device's trust store. Without one of those, TLS is still doing its job. It becomes a finding when paired with what the unpinned channel actually carries.
Lack of certificate pinning is a hardening step and does not constitute a vulnerability on its own.

info.title: Task hijacking (StrandHogg) possible on Android 10 and lower
info.description: minSdkVersion 22 lets the app run on Android versions before 11, and its task affinity is its package name "edu.ksu.cs.benign". There, another app can declare the same affinity, with allowTaskReparenting, and have its own activity shown in this app's task.
info.impact: On a device running Android 10 or lower, a malicious app can put a look-alike screen on top of this app's task, phishing credentials or keeping the real app from being shown.
info.recommendation: Raise minSdkVersion to 30, where Android fixed this. Until then, android:taskAffinity="" on the <application> mitigates the original attack, though not its runtime variant on unpatched Android 9 and lower.

reasons: Does not establish that any activity displaying sensitive information is targetable.
